Have a coffee with Lorraine.

reward.note: The Millbrook Clarion, page one, above the fold: 'COFFEE MACHINE IS: WORKING.' Below the fold: the Lumber Kings.

quests.hooks: The Hot Stove (DECOR 1.3: the dented machine and the flip sign), concessions, the cleaning job, the Clarion.

quests.title: Hot Choc Late
quests.prompt: Lorraine, the menu board's still missing two letters.
quests.summary: The felt menu board reads HOT CHOC LATE because two letters fell off years ago. Nobody fixes it, because it's true at public skate.

steps.text: Ask Bev if she still has the felt letters from her old shop sign.

on_done.note: Bev: 'A tin of felt letters from 1979. Lots of E's. One O. Nobody ever needs the O. Take the tin, champ.'

steps.text: Decide what the menu board says.
Run a public skate and see who orders what.
See how the menu went over.

quests.hooks: The Hot Stove menu board (DECOR 1.3, exact text), Bev's shop, public skate concessions, a small keepsake-style choice.

quests.title: Forty-One Days
quests.prompt: Marg, you're staring at the days-since sign again.
quests.summary: The plant room sign reads DAYS SINCE No. 1 TRIPPED, and the record painted underneath is 41, from 1996. Marg would like a new number to paint.

steps.text: Keep the plant log: twenty morning rounds, written in pencil, no gaps.
Change No. 1's oil. Half the sight glass, not full.
Descale the condenser so No. 1 isn't fighting the roof.
Twenty more rounds. The last stretch is where Gus lost it in 1997.
Bring Marg the log.

quests.hooks: Plant rounds and the log (RINK_SIM 3.1), oil and descale mini games 4.2 and 4.6, the days-since sign keepsake (DECOR 1.13), Marg's red pen (marg_red_pen).

quests.title: The Ghost in the Binder
quests.prompt: Dylan, why are you whispering in the plant room?
quests.summary: New notes in Gus's handwriting keep appearing on the plant room binder. Gus is in Florida. Dylan thinks the binder is haunted.

steps.text: Look at the binder on the plant room door.

on_done.note: A new sticky note, Gus's capitals, the marker still wet: DYLAN. THE SQUEEGEE. G. Gus has been in Florida since spring.

steps.text: Do the next three morning rounds and watch for new notes.

on_done.note: Another one: WHOEVER LEFT THE BAY LIGHT ON. G. Also wet. Also impossible.

steps.text: Look around the resurfacer bay.

on_done.note: Behind the drawer marked DORIS (DON'T): a pad of yellow sticky notes and a black marker, the cap chewed flat.

steps.text: Ask Earl about the marker.

on_done.note: Earl: 'Gus left me his capitals. Forty years of watching him write. Easier than saying it myself. You'd listen to Gus.'

steps.text: Tell Dylan something.

quests.hooks: Gus's binder (readables gus_binder), plant rounds, the resurfacer bay drawers, Earl and Dylan's relationship, a keepsake note.

quests.title: Most Improved, 1991
quests.prompt: Gary, you're stopping in front of the lost and found on purpose.
quests.summary: A small trophy, MOST IMPROVED 1991, has sat unclaimed in the lost and found for thirty-five years. Gary, who learned to stop last February and has an award named after him, wants to know whose it is.

steps.text: Find the trophy in the lost and found crate at the rental window.

on_done.note: Small, plastic gold, a skater on top with one arm missing. MOST IMPROVED 1991. ADULT LEARN TO SKATE. No name.

steps.text: Ask Midge Kaminski to check the Clarion archive for 1991.

on_done.note: Midge: 'March 1991, page 6. Adult Learn to Skate graduates. Most Improved: Mrs D. Vachon, 40, who could not stand in January.'

steps.text: Ask Doreen Vachon about 1991.

on_done.note: Doreen: 'I left it in the lost and found on purpose, dear. In 1991. I was embarrassed. Forty years old and a trophy for standing up. I'm not embarrassed any more. Give it to the boy.'

steps.text: Tell Gary whose it is.

quests.hooks: Lost and found (readables: the Most Improved 1991 mini mystery), the Clarion archive, adult learn-to-skate history, the trophy case.

quests.title: Whose Leg Is It?
quests.prompt: Mrs Mulroney, the conservator's letter came.
quests.summary: The lobby mural's restorer wants to know whether to correct the three-legged skater. Agnes, who taught the class that painted it, wants to know whose legs they are first.

steps.text: Get the building far enough along for the conservator to start: a facility score of 40.
Ask Dale Huffman which leg was his.

on_done.note: Dale: 'I've never said. It's a bylaw of the heart. Ask the girl in the red toque. She was holding the other brush.'

steps.text: Ask Bev about the girl in the red toque.

on_done.note: Bev: 'The left one's Dale's. He painted it backwards. The right one's mine. That's not me in the toque, champ. Fine. It's me. Don't tell Agnes I said so.'

steps.text: Decide what the conservator does with the third leg.
Give Agnes the answer.

quests.hooks: The mural Winter on the Mill Pond (DECOR 1.2: the three legs and Gus's Florida, keepsake rules), lobby renovation, a keepsake choice.

quests.title: The Last Brass Strip
quests.prompt: Midge, you're reading the dedication plaque again.
quests.summary: Below WE'RE TRYING on the dedication plaque is a gap the exact size of one more brass strip, left on purpose for whoever fixes the roof properly.

steps.text: Read the dedication plaque between the front doors.

on_done.note: ROOF REPAIRED 1991, 1998, 2004, 2011, 2017. WE'RE TRYING. And under it, a clean rectangle of bronze the size of one more strip.

steps.text: Renovate the roof properly: membrane and insulation, the March drip gone.
Ask June Penner to engrave the strip at Penner Hardware.

on_done.note: June: 'Grandpa engraved the first strip in 1991 on that same machine. It still works if you talk to it.'

steps.text: Screw the strip into the gap on the plaque.
Tell Midge it's up.

reward.note: The Millbrook Clarion, Off the Boards: 'The Strip.' Midge Kaminski's column runs to two pages. The letters page is empty that week for the first time since 1998.

quests.hooks: The dedication plaque keepsake (readables dedication_plaque, DECOR 2), the roof renovation (RINK_SIM 5.8), Penner Hardware, the Clarion. Needs the renovation system to set roof_renovated.

favours.title: Earlier Ice for {known_as}
favours.summary: {name} wants Saturday's minor hockey practice to run on time so the family can make a tournament in Kessler.
favours.ask: Any chance Saturday practice starts on time? Exactly on time? We've got a game in Kessler at noon and the Kessler road is the Kessler road, {owner}.
favours.thanks: On the dot. We made Kessler with time for a coffee. You don't know what that means to a hockey family. It means everything.

steps.text: Run a minor hockey session on decent ice, on time.

favours.hooks: Minor hockey schedule reliability; the schedule pressure source (PATHS 1.3).

favours.title: A Fresh Flood for {known_as}'s Kid
favours.summary: {name}'s child has a figure test and needs a flood right before.
favours.ask: My daughter has her test on Saturday. Could the ice be flooded right before? Not an hour before. Right before. She says she can feel an hour.
favours.thanks: Fresh as snow. She passed, and she says it was the ice. I say it was her. We're both right.

steps.text: Flood right before the test.
Hold the test session on ice rated 65 or better.

favours.hooks: Resurface job, figure_show rating, figure parents' loyalty.

favours.title: Lights Down for {known_as}
favours.summary: {name} would like the lights down for one slow song at public skate.
favours.ask: Could you dim the lights for one slow song at public skate? We're celebrating. Don't ask what. Fine. It's our third date. Third dates are big.
favours.thanks: One song, lights low, and nobody fell. Well, we fell. On purpose. Thank you.

steps.text: Run a public skate on good ice and dim the lamps for one song.

favours.hooks: Public skate atmosphere, house lights, date_night attendance.

favours.title: One Lap with {known_as}
favours.summary: {name} would like the owner to hold their hand for one lap at learn-to-skate.
favours.ask: This is embarrassing. Would you hold my hand for one lap? Just one. The instructor's busy with Gary Pruett's cousin, and he's a lot.
favours.thanks: One whole lap. I didn't fall. You were very brave about my grip. Sorry about your fingers.

steps.text: Get your skates on and meet them on the ice.
Skate the lap during a learn-to-skate session.

favours.hooks: Learn-to-skate, the owner on the ice, the adult beginners' confidence.

favours.title: {known_as} Rides Doris
favours.summary: {name} wants to ride along on one flood.
favours.ask: Can I ride on Doris? One flood. I'll sit so still. I'll sit stiller than anybody's ever sat. Earl says ask you. Earl said it like he wanted you to say no. Say yes.
favours.thanks: I RODE DORIS. She pulled left when the tank got heavy, just like Earl said. I'm never washing this hat.

steps.text: Do a flood with them riding along.

favours.hooks: Doris and the resurface job, rink rats, Earl's protectiveness.

favours.title: {known_as}'s Mitten
favours.summary: {name} has lost a mitten, probably in the lost and found.
favours.ask: I've lost a mitten, dear. Left one. Brown, with a cuff. My sister knitted it in 1988. It'll be in your crate with all the others, poor things.
favours.thanks: That's it! That's the one. Oh, you're a good egg. My sister would have liked you. She liked very few people.

steps.text: Check the lost and found crate at the rental window.

favours.hooks: Lost and found, regulars' goodwill.

favours.title: The Wrong Bag
favours.summary: {name} took the wrong hockey bag home on Thursday.
favours.ask: So I took the wrong bag home Thursday. Same colour, same tape. Different jock. Mine's still here somewhere. Could you look in the dressing room? I can't, the other guy's there and it's awkward.
favours.thanks: That's my bag. That's my smell. Thanks. I'll get the other guy's back to him. Probably by Thursday.

steps.text: Look in the dressing rooms for the right bag.

favours.hooks: Dressing rooms, the notice board's 'wrong bag' line.

favours.title: A Clean Sheet for {known_as}
favours.summary: {name} would like a fresh sheet before stick and puck.
favours.ask: Any chance of a flood before stick and puck? The beer league chewed it up last night. It's like stickhandling on a gravel road.
favours.thanks: Glass. Pure glass. I did forty minutes of toe drags and nobody watched. Perfect.

steps.text: Flood before stick and puck.
Run the stick and puck session.

favours.hooks: Resurface job, stick and puck in dead time.

favours.title: Salt the Lot
favours.summary: {name} says the parking lot is icier than the rink.
favours.ask: Your parking lot is a better skating rink than your skating rink. Not the good kind. We're in sneakers. Could somebody salt it before Wednesday?
favours.thanks: Walked from the car to the door without falling once. A broomball first. We celebrated by falling on the ice instead.

steps.text: Check the parking lot.
Clean up and salt the walkways.

favours.hooks: Parking lot, cleaning job, broomball goodwill.

favours.title: Heat for Section B
favours.summary: {name} says the heater over their seats is out for the Lumber Kings game.
favours.ask: The heater over B row four's been dead since the opener. Forty years I've sat there for the Kings. I can take a loss. I can't take a loss and frostbite.
favours.thanks: Toasty. We lost, but toasty. That's the best kind of loss.

steps.text: Check the heater over their seats.
Run the next Lumber Kings home game.

favours.hooks: Stands heaters (DECOR 1.10), senior hockey attendance.

favours.title: A Spot at the Glass
favours.summary: {name} wants to stand at the glass during pro practice.
favours.ask: When the Dukes practise, can I stand at the glass by the bench? I won't bang on it. I've got a pen and a puck and a plan.
favours.thanks: Three signatures and a stick tap! A STICK TAP. Through the glass. I felt it in my teeth.

steps.text: Let them watch a Dukes practice from the glass.

favours.hooks: Pro practice, autograph hunters, the glass as a place.

favours.title: Coffee for the Coach in the Stands
favours.summary: {name} won't leave the glass during the game and would like a coffee brought over.
favours.ask: Bring me a coffee to the glass? Double-double. If I leave, the coach'll play my kid on the fourth line. He'll do that anyway. But I'll know.
favours.thanks: Hot. Sweet. He played my kid on the fourth line. I didn't yell. Much. The coffee helped.

steps.text: Grab a coffee from the Hot Stove.
Bring it to the glass.

favours.hooks: The canteen, the glass, coffee coaches (PEOPLE 5).

favours.title: A Warm Seat for {known_as}
favours.summary: {name} wants a seat near a working heater for a grandchild's game.
favours.ask: A seat under a heater for my grandson's game? These knees came to watch, not to suffer. And if you could point me at the one that works, I'd be grateful.
favours.thanks: Warm knees, and he scored. Well, he was on the ice when someone scored. Close enough.

steps.text: Find a seat under a working heater.
Run the minor hockey game.

favours.hooks: Stands, minor hockey family attendance.

favours.title: Coffee at Shift Change
favours.summary: {name} comes off a shift at the mill and wants the canteen open early.
favours.ask: I'm off the night shift at six. Any chance the Hot Stove's got coffee on before the doors open? Just a pot. I'll pay double. I'll pay in coins, but double.
favours.thanks: Coffee at six. You're doing the Lord's work. Or the mill's. Same thing in this valley.

steps.text: Get a pot on at the Hot Stove early.

favours.hooks: Canteen hours, shift workers at odd hours.

favours.title: Something From This Century
favours.summary: {name} would like public skate to play something newer than the Casio's repertoire.
favours.ask: Can public skate play something from this century? Doreen's organ is great. It's very great. It's so great. Please.
favours.thanks: They played my song. Doreen played it on Organ 2. It was terrible. It was the best thing I've ever heard.

steps.text: Run a public skate with a request or two.

favours.hooks: Public skate music, teens at the rink, Doreen.

favours.title: The East Circle
favours.summary: {name} says there's a rut where they land their jumps.
favours.ask: There's a rut on the east circle, right where I land my loop. I've fallen on it four times. I'm not blaming the rut. I'm blaming the rut a little.
favours.thanks: Landed it! Clean! No rut! I'm telling Hélène. She'll nod. That's a lot, from her.

steps.text: Flood the rut out.
Get figure ice rated 65 or better.

favours.hooks: Ice ratings for figure use, resurface job, the figure club's 'never forgives a rut at a jump landing'.

favours.title: The Lucky Glove
favours.summary: {name} can't find their other glove, the lucky one with the hole.
favours.ask: I can't find my other glove. The one with the hole. It's my lucky hole. Mom says it's not lucky, it's a hole. She's wrong.
favours.thanks: MY HOLE. I mean my glove. Thank you. We're going to win now. Probably.

steps.text: Look for the glove in the dressing rooms.

favours.hooks: Dressing rooms, minor players, lost and found flavour.

favours.title: A Table for the 50/50
favours.summary: {name} needs a table in the lobby to sell 50/50 tickets on game night.
favours.ask: Could I have a table in the lobby for the 50/50 on game night? Not THE TABLE, I'm not a monster. Any table. The drum's heavy.
favours.thanks: Four hundred and twelve dollars in the drum, and a man from Kessler won it. We'll never hear the end of it. Thank you.

steps.text: Set up a table in the lobby.
Run the game night.

favours.hooks: Lobby, game nights, the 50/50 drum (DECOR 1.15).

favours.title: Water for the Officials
favours.summary: {name} would like water bottles for the officials before a game.
favours.ask: Any chance of a few bottles of water for the officials? The tap in the ref room runs brown for a minute, then it runs beige. Beige isn't a colour you drink.
favours.thanks: Clear water. I could see through it. The incident book will hear about this, in a good way.

steps.text: Grab some water from the Hot Stove.
Run the game.

favours.hooks: Officials' goodwill, the ref room tap, the incident book.

favours.title: A Quiet Seat
favours.summary: {name} would like a quiet seat away from the rafters end, and a line sheet.
favours.ask: A quiet seat, away from the rafters end, and a line sheet if anyone has one. I'm not here. You didn't see me. Nice ice, by the way. I didn't say that either.
favours.thanks: Good seat. Good sheet. I saw what I came to see. I can't tell you what it was. Thank you.

steps.text: Find a quiet seat in the stands.
Run the game they came to watch.

favours.hooks: Scouts at senior games, the stands, a hint of the hockey career.
